fine_lines.title: scalding vs scorching
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلاهما يعني حارًّا جدًا. scalding للسوائل مثل الماء والقهوة. scorching للطقس وحرارة الشمس.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean very hot. Scalding is for liquids (water, coffee). Scorching is for weather and the sun.

examples.sentence: Don't touch the water; it's scalding.
It was a scorching day in August.

fine_lines.title: rich vs wealthy
fine_lines.explanation_ar: rich غنيّ. wealthy أقوى: ثريّ جدًا، مثل الشخص الذي يدفع رواتب الأغنياء.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Rich = has a lot of money. Wealthy is stronger: very rich, like the person who pays rich people.

examples.sentence: The wealthy owner of the team pays him.

fine_lines.title: rapid vs rapidly
fine_lines.explanation_ar: rapid صفة تأتي قبل الاسم: a rapid speaker. rapidly ظرف يصف الفعل: He speaks rapidly.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Rapid is an adjective (a rapid change). Rapidly is an adverb (it changed rapidly).

examples.sentence: There was a rapid change in the weather.

grammar.title: Replace "very + adjective" with one strong adjective
grammar.explanation_ar: بدل تكرار very مع الصفة، استخدم صفة واحدة قوية تحمل معنى very. لا تقل very exhausted أو very freezing لأن هذه الصفات قوية بذاتها؛ يمكنك أن تقول absolutely أو rather بدلًا من ذلك.
grammar.explanation_en: Instead of very + adjective, use one strong adjective that already means "very". Don't say "very exhausted" or "very freezing"; these words are already strong. You can use "absolutely" or "rather" instead.
